rosmara_cat_1.m: Well, you see, he's my guard cat.

rosmara_cat_2.m: Yes. If you attempt to rob me, he'll attack you. Hence he is my guard cat.

rosmara_cat_3.m: No, not seroiusly. He guards my fruits and vegetables.

rosmara_cat_4.m: I have a business agreement with him. He guards my food from the rats in exchange for a place to sleep.
r: Oh, why didn't you just say so?
Well, he's not holding up his end of the deal, because there's a rat behind your tent right now.

rosmara_cat_5.m: I wanted to waste your time just as you are doing to my time. Walking up to my business counter asking about my cat! Get lost, kid.

rosmara_explain.m: This is my place of business. Right here on the side of Duleian Road.
r: Why here? There's nothing else here besides you.

rosmara_explain_10.m: What kind of fog are you talking about?
r: The fog that the witch had created in the swamp, of course.
The fog further down the road behind the kobolds, of course.

rosmara_explain_11.m: Are you still afraid of witches or fog, child?
r: I am not a child anymore!!
I was with the witch! Without me the fog would still be there!

rosmara_explain_11a.m: Are you still afraid of kobolds or fog, child?
r: I am not a child anymore!!
I have mastered the fog and survived the kobolds!!

rosmara_explain_12.m: Yes, of course. Calm down, child.

rosmara_explain_2.m: Oh, you silly child. This is a very well traveled road. All the people coming and going from and to Feygard. It's a long road and they get hungry.
r: OK, you sell food. What kind of food?
And the fog? No one could take the path anymore.

rosmara_explain_3.m: I sell things that a child such as yourself is most likely not interested in.
r: I am not a child anymore!!
As an adult, I am interested in seeing what you have.
Where do you get these fruits and vegetables?

rosmara_explain_5.m: From all over Dhayavar, but mostly from the great farmers in Loneford.
r: Oh, yeah. I've seen all of their great farms.

rosmara_heartsteel_10.m: Yes, yes you are and a foolhardy one at that.

rosmara_heartsteel_20.m: Carrying the very same weapon Geomyr banned?

rosmara_initial_phrase.m: How can I help you today?
r: What is going on with that cat?
Do you know why the village of Wexlow is void of people?
I would like to make a purchase, please.

rosmara_wexlow.m: What?! There's nobody in the village?
r: Nope. Not a single person, and it looks like there hasn't been for a while.

rosmara_wexlow2.m: Hmm, I hope they are all right.

feygard_nondisplayed.3: The PC has attacked Gamjee the troll under the village of Wexlow without knowing that Gamjee has those villagers held captive.
feygard_nondisplayed.4: The PC has attacked Gamjee the troll under the village of Wexlow after learning that Gamjee has those villagers held captive.
feygard_nondisplayed.5: The PC has attacked Gamjee the troll under the village of Wexlow.
feygard_nondisplayed.6: Gamjee, the troll under the village of Wexlow has sent the villager back to Wexlow.
feygard_nondisplayed.7: PC gave Godwin, a villager from Wexlow, his lost ring. [wrapper for 13, 14, 15]
feygard_nondisplayed.13: PC gave Godwin, a villager from Wexlow, his lost ring for free.
feygard_nondisplayed.14: PC gave Godwin, a villager from Wexlow, his lost ring for 2k gold.
feygard_nondisplayed.15: PC gave Godwin, a villager from Wexlow, his lost ring for 3k gold.
feygard_nondisplayed.8: PC learns that Rosmara sells fruits and vegetables
feygard_nondisplayed.9: PC can sleep in Wexlow Village.
feygard_nondisplayed.10: PC has learned what the beekeeper, Leofric does for work.

echoes_of_enchantment.1: At the Wexlow well, I angered something evil and powerful (named Gamjee, I think) to the point that it pulled me down into the well. I've landed at the well's bottom severely injured, but alive.
echoes_of_enchantment.2: After I landed with a thud at the bottom of the well and being concussed, I began to hear sounds off in the distance. Were they voices? Were they even real? Maybe a symptom of the concussion perhaps?
echoes_of_enchantment.3: After I landed with a thud at the bottom of the well and being concussed, I began to hear sounds off in the distance. Were they voices? Were they even real? Are they the voices of something more sinister?
echoes_of_enchantment.4: The voices I thought I heard earlier seem to be persistent and seemed to be getting louder. It was hard to tell if they're real or just a figment of my imagination.
echoes_of_enchantment.5: Deep inside the well's tunnels, I found eight people being held captive inside a very deep pit.
echoes_of_enchantment.6: I learned that these people are held captive by a troll and they need me to find a way to free them.
echoes_of_enchantment.7: I met the troll named Gamjee and listened to what he had to say.
echoes_of_enchantment.8: In an attempt to help Gamjee and the villagers, I have facilitated a conversation between Gamjee and one of the villagers.
echoes_of_enchantment.9: I killed Gamjee and in doing so, I found a rope that I think might be helpful in freeing those people in that pit.
echoes_of_enchantment.11: I killed Gamjee and in doing so, I realized that I really should go investigate the voices I heard earlier.
echoes_of_enchantment.10: The villagers have been freed. I should visit them back in their village of Wexlow.
echoes_of_enchantment.12: The villagers and Gamjee agreed to a schedule for using the well, ensuring everyone has access to water without conflict. But the villagers are still in the pit.
echoes_of_enchantment.13: After the villagers and Gamjee agreed to a compromise, Gamjee gave me a rope and instructed me to use it to free the remaining villagers in the pit.
echoes_of_enchantment.14: I've visited the people of Wexlow Village after they made it home. They are happy to sleep in their own beds now.

loneford.10: I heard a story about Loneford. Apparently, a lot of people have become ill there recently, and some have even died. The cause is still unknown.
loneford.11: I should investigate what could have caused the people of Loneford to become ill. To gather clues, I should ask the citizens of Loneford and the surrounding areas about what they think is the cause.
loneford.21: The guards in the Crossroads guardhouse are certain that the illness in Loneford is caused by some sabotage done by the priests or people from Nor City.
loneford.22: Some villagers in Loneford believe that the illness is caused by the guards from Feygard, in some scheme to make the people suffer even more than they already have.
loneford.23: Talion, the chapel priest in Loneford, thinks that the illness is the work of the Shadow, as punishment for Loneford's lack of devotion to the Shadow.
loneford.24: Taevinn in Loneford is certain that Sienn in the southeast barn has something to do with the illness. Apparently, Sienn keeps a pet around that has approached Taevinn in a threatening manner several times.
loneford.25: I should go see Landa in the Loneford tavern. Rumor has it that he saw something that he doesn't dare tell anyone.
loneford.30: Landa confused me with someone else at first. He apparently saw a boy doing something around the town well during the night before the illness started. He was scared to talk to me at first since he thought I looked like the boy he had seen. Could it have been Andor that he saw?
loneford.31: Also, the night after he saw the boy at the well, he saw Buceth taking samples of the water in the well. Strangely enough, Buceth has not gotten ill like the others in the village.
loneford.35: I should go question Buceth at the Loneford chapel about what he was doing at the well, and about whether he knows anything about Andor.
loneford.41: I have bribed Buceth into talking to me.
loneford.42: I have told Buceth that I am ready to follow the Shadow.
loneford.45: Buceth tells me that he is assigned by the priests in Nor City to make sure the Shadow casts its glow over Loneford. Apparently, the priests had sent a boy to do some business in Loneford, and Buceth was tasked with gathering some samples from the water well.
loneford.50: I have attacked Buceth. I should bring any evidence that Buceth has on him to Kuldan, the guard captain in the longhouse in Loneford.
loneford.54: I have given the vial that Buceth had on him to Kuldan, the guard captain in Loneford.
loneford.55: Kuldan thanked me for solving the mystery of the illness in Loneford. They will start bringing in water with help from Feygard instead of drinking from the well from now on. Kuldan also told me to visit the castle steward in Feygard if I want to help further.
loneford.60: I have promised to keep Buceth's story a secret. If Andor was indeed here, he must have had a good reason for doing what he did. Buceth also told me to visit the chapel custodian in Nor City if I want to learn more about the Shadow.

fogmonster.5: You had entered a very unnatural looking fog and decided to find the source of it. Maybe you could lift the fog?
fogmonster.10: After you chased away a fog monster, the fog suddenly dissipated.
fogmonster.20: Another fog monster guarded the footbridge to the hut. As long as there was still fog somewhere around the hut, you couldn't drive it away.
fogmonster.30: In the hut you encountered a terrifying looking witch.
fogmonster.70: You defeated the old witch in battle, so she can't create a new fog.
fogmonster.80: You were able to convince the witch Mim to keep the road clear of fog.
fogmonster.90: You convinced the witch Mim to replace the fog with a distraction spell.
fogmonster.92: Madame Mim gave you a bottle of her swamp water.
